title: Costco Partners With SCAN Group to Sell Medicare Advantage Plans
excerpt: The warehouse giant will offer co-branded Medicare products in two states, leveraging its 82 million members and trusted brand to enter the more than $600 billion Medicare market.
body:
• Costco and nonprofit insurer SCAN Group announced a partnership to sell co-branded Medicare Advantage and Medicare supplement plans, starting with a limited rollout in three states.
  • The target markets encompass roughly 5 million Medicare enrollees, with plans to integrate Costco pharmacy, optical and hearing services into the coverage.
  • The move enters a $600 billion-plus national Medicare market at a time when other insurers are retreating from Medicare Advantage and trimming benefits amid rising costs.
  • Costco stock reclaimed a key technical level on Tuesday following the announcement.

Costco Wholesale announced Tuesday that it will begin selling store-branded Medicare plans through a partnership with SCAN Group, a Long Beach, California-based nonprofit insurer, marking the warehouse giant's entry into one of the largest and fastest-changing segments of American healthcare.

The companies will start with a limited rollout: jointly branded Medicare Advantage products in two states and a Medicare supplement plan in a third, covering markets with about 5 million Medicare enrollees. Specific locations and timing were not disclosed, pending regulatory approval from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

Leveraging Trust at Scale

SCAN CEO Sachin Jain framed the deal as a bet on Costco's consumer credibility. "As a longtime Costco customer, I know that if I walk into a Costco store, I'm just going to buy the item because they've done the work for me to make sure that it's a high-quality, high-value product," Jain said. "That's what seniors are increasingly looking for in their Medicare experience."

"Costco has built something exceedingly rare: trust at scale. Its members believe that if Costco puts its name on something, it has been carefully vetted for quality and value. That is exactly the kind of trust healthcare desperately needs."

— Sachin Jain, CEO of SCAN Group

The plans will be sold in Costco stores, through insurance agents and online — but will not include a Costco membership, which federal rules prohibit bundling with Medicare products. Future offerings may include redesigned pharmacy benefits, a Medicare Flex Card with over-the-counter benefits, and vision and audiology products, pending regulatory review.

Entering a Squeezed Market

The partnership comes against a challenging backdrop for Medicare Advantage. The private-plan alternative to traditional Medicare now covers more than half of all Medicare beneficiaries nationwide, but rising costs and changing billing rules have squeezed insurers. Several major providers have curtailed markets and trimmed benefits in recent years. Earlier this month, CMS ended a temporary program that helped keep Part D prescription-drug premiums in check.

"SCAN clearly views this collaboration as a way for it to reach more consumers. And that makes sense. Costco is a household name, which SCAN isn't," said Matthew Fiedler, senior fellow in health policy at the Brookings Institution. He noted the arrangement likely involves Costco receiving commissions for plan sign-ups, a standard practice in Medicare Advantage distribution.

Building on an Existing Relationship

SCAN and Costco are not starting from scratch. SCAN already lists Costco as a preferred pharmacy, offering competitive prices on medications and vaccinations to its approximately 560,000 Medicare Advantage members across six states: Arizona, California, Nevada, New Mexico, Texas and Washington. Members can use eyewear allowances at Costco locations, and a rewards program lets some enrollees earn up to $125 for completing health-related activities, redeemable at Costco for groceries, personal care products or fitness equipment.

Costco CEO Ron Vachris said the deal extends the company's decades-long pattern of expanding into adjacent services. "Selecting SCAN as our partner to deliver a better healthcare experience for seniors is an extension of that commitment," Vachris said in a statement.

Market Reaction and Outlook

Costco stock moved higher Tuesday following the news, reclaiming a key technical level. William Blair analyst Phillip Blee characterized Costco as a "consistent, defensive operator," noting that U.S. clubs posted 6.9% adjusted comparable-store sales growth in July.

The co-branded Medicare play follows a model other insurers have used: UnitedHealthcare, for example, partners with AARP to sell Medicare Advantage products under the advocacy group's name. A previous Medicare Advantage partnership between UnitedHealthcare and Walmart ended two years ago. Whether Costco's powerful brand loyalty translates to healthcare decisions will be the test.
nri_angle: The partnership could benefit aging Indian-American families navigating Medicare, particularly in California, Texas and other states with large diaspora populations where both Costco and SCAN operate.
